newsitem.title: USA: Navigation curbs on lower Mississippi cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Navigation curbs on lower Mississippi cancelled.

text.p: The Coast Guard has repealed most restrictions to maritime transit on the lower Mississippi River due to a steady drop in water levels, officials said on Monday.
The curbs, including strict tow-size to horsepower ratio requirements and limits on the transit of hazardous chemical cargoes, were eliminated at 0100 EDT/0500 GMT this morning, they said.

"All the restrictions that we had on the river were cancelled last night at midnight (central daylight time)," said chief petty officer Neal Powell with the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in New Orleans.
"The only thing that remains in effect is a safety zone for Baton Rouge for downbound tugs," he added.

The Baton Rouge safety zone affects a 13-mile stretch of the river, Powell said. In that area, vessels are required to remain 2,000 feet apart, and overtaking other ships is not permitted. Additional horsepower requirements also remain in effect.
On the remaining 437-mile span of the lower Mississippi through Southwest Pass, all horsepower and daylight-only restrictions have been set aside, Powell said.

"The river continues to fall," he added, with water levels hovering near 14.5 feet in New Orleans Monday morning. The lower Mississippi has fallen at a rate of 0.1 to 0.2 feet per day since cresting at 16.9 feet two weeks ago.
